title: Define incremental compatibility signatures and soft-pin windows for staggered onboarding of community models
creator: Lena Morales
description: Purpose: remove ambiguity in the intake flow for new community/open models by specifying a compact, machine-readable compatibility signature plus an operational "soft-pin" window that enables staggered rollout and controlled rollback. This ticket captures the product requirements, acceptance criteria, and proposed thresholds so engineering and design can implement runtime checks, console UX, and onboarding docs.
background_and_rationale: We currently accept a freeform compatibility note on catalog entries which causes inconsistent runtime routing and frequent P0 churn when models surface unexpected kernel/quant issues. The compatibility signature will standardize key runtime attributes (tokenizer id, kv-cache semantics, eager kv offsets, preferred quant formats, max-context stable test) and allow the platform to make deterministic routing decisions. Soft-pin windows let us accept unpinned variants for a short probation period while monitoring regressions, reducing blocker spikes for community submissions.
requirements_summary: 1) Define a JSON schema for a "compatibility signature" that model submitters and onboarding engineers must populate. 2) Define the lifecycle and semantics of a "soft-pin" window (defaults, maximum length, opt-out). 3) Specify automatic health and quality triggers that will convert a soft-pin into a hard pin, extend the window, or roll back the variant. 4) Surface this state & signals in the Console and catalog UI.
soft_pin_semantics: Auto-extend on low-confidence metrics: +7 days max
Soft-pin means: runtime will prefer pinned stable variant but will accept soft-pinned variant for sampled production traffic (configurable sampling)
Soft-pin can be requested by submitter or set by intake reviewer
Opt-out allowed only for enterprise customers with explicit SLA negotiation
health_triggers_and_thresholds: Latency regression > 20% vs baseline over 24h -> immediate rollback to previous pinned variant
Failure rate increase > 0.75 percentage points absolute over baseline in 1h -> rollback and alert
Quality signal: eval BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity drop > 3 points on steward prompt-set -> mark as high-risk and pause rollout
Memory OOMs or kernel crashes (>=1 per 10k requests) -> immediate quarantine
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility signature schema published in Confluence and added to model intake form
Runtime accepts and validates compatibility signatures on ingest and publishes parse/validation errors to intake logs
Console shows soft-pin state, start/end dates, sampling rate, and key health metrics for the variant
Automated smoke tests run against the declared example_smoke_tokens and results are saved to the model entry before a soft-pin can be created
Defined rollback runbook exists with runbook link in the model entry
E2E test in runtime repo demonstrating auto-rollback triggers (latency and failure scenarios)
Documentation for contributors explaining how to create signature and request soft-pin
out_of_scope: Full rewrite of model catalog UI
Automated remediation for quality issues beyond rollback (e.g., retraining guidance)
Making soft-pin the default for all internal/enterprise submissions without explicit opt-in configuration
decisions_made: Use a compact JSON schema for compat signatures rather than freeform tags
Soft-pin windows are time-limited with a configurable extend-on-success policy
Health triggers will be defined conservatively and can be tuned after 2 pilot onboardings
open_questions: What sampling rates should be the console default for public vs enterprise tiers?
Should we require contributor attestation for quantization artifacts?
How to handle multi-variant submissions (several quantized builds) under a single signature?
Should baseline metrics be provided by submitter or bootstrapped by the intake pipeline?
